title: Unique binary search trees
statement: Return how many structurally different BSTs store the values 1..n (n ≤ 19).
hints: Choose the root i: then the left subtree uses i − 1 values and the right n − i.
G(n) = Σ G(i − 1)·G(n − i): the Catalan recurrence, closed form C(2n, n)/(n + 1).
complexity: O(n²) DP or O(n) closed form

solution.explanation: The DP over the root choice gives the Catalan recurrence. Recognising Catalan numbers (1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, …) lets you jump to the closed form, and tells you the same count answers balanced parentheses, triangulations of a polygon, Dyck paths and stack-sortable permutations. Spotting a known sequence by computing the first few terms is a legitimate interview technique.
solution.cpp: long long numTrees(int n) { vector<long long> g(n + 1, 0); g[0] = 1; for (int k = 1; k <= n; k++) for (int i = 1; i <= k; i++) g[k] += g[i-1] * g[k-i]; return g[n]; }
